1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 g6 4.O-O Bg7 5.c.strategy: Solves the problem of e4 at once, since the queen defends it along the fourth rank, and adds a second attacker to the knight on c6 behind the bishop. White keeps the pressure on the knight while the pawn centre stays intact.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 g6 4.O-O Bg7 5.c.name: Sicilian Defence: Nyezhmetdinov-Rossolimo Attack, Fianchetto Variation, Totsky Attack

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 g6 4.O-O Bg7 5.c.strategy: A gambit: with e4 still unprotected, White opens the centre at once and leaves both d4 and e4 under attack. The compensation is piece activity and the threat of taking on c6, and it is risky, since White has to make up the lost material.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 g6 4.O-O Bg7 5.c.name: Sicilian Defence: Nyezhmetdinov-Rossolimo Attack, Fianchetto Variation, Lutikov Gambit
